trial_court: Family Court, case number not mentioned
case_name: Sudha Gupta vs Har Prasad Gupta
facts_of_case: The parties got married in 1993. The wife does not want to resume cohabitation with the husband due to strained relationship. She had previously contested a petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: A decree for restitution of conjugal rights is a stepping stone towards divorce.
legal_principles.held: Thus, the legal position is that on passing of a decree for restitution of conjugal rights at the most it can be said that the law enforces cohabitation but it does not and cannot enforce sexual intercourse.
cited_cases: Smt. Saroj Rani Vs. Sudarshan Kumar Chadha, (1984) SC 1562

legal_principles.principle: If a decree for restitution of conjugal rights is not complied with for a period of one year, it becomes a ground to seek dissolution of marriage.
legal_principles.held: Section 13(1A)(ii) provides that if the withdrawing spouse is disobedient to the decree of restitution of conjugal rights and the husband and wife continue to live separately as before, each of them is entitled to seek dissolution of marriage.
cited_cases: Smt. Saroj Rani Vs. Sudarshan Kumar Chadha, (1984) SC 1562

legal_principles.principle: The law does not enforce sexual intercourse, only cohabitation.
legal_principles.held: The object of decree for restitution of conjugal rights is to bring about cohabitation between the parties so that they can live at the matrimonial home in amity. If the decree for restitution of conjugal rights is not complied with for a period of one year it becomes a ground to seek dissolution of marriage under Section 13(1A)(ii) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
cited_cases: Smt. Saroj Rani Vs. Sudarshan Kumar Chadha, (1984) SC 1562

legal_principles.principle: The legal position is that the defaulting spouse tries to denounce the restitution of conjugal rights but welcome as a ground for seeking dissolution of marriage.
legal_principles.held: The legal position which emerges is that while the defaulting spouse tries to denounce the restitution of conjugal rights but welcome as a ground for seeking dissolution of marriage under Section 13(1A) (ii) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
cited_cases: Smt. Saroj Rani Vs. Sudarshan Kumar Chadha, (1984) SC 1562
